case.title: Undo cannot move back a work order that was invoiced in the meantime
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682428 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682428 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has a work order {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A}, with status Complete (all lines complete and reviewed, not invoiced) and no shift booked on the Schedule. {Technician-B} is not the technician on any of its lines.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682428 Undo Invoiced and {Work-order-1} is S2-37461.
  • Two browser windows are open side by side, both signed in as you: window 1 on the starting screen below, window 2 on {Work-order-1}'s "Finance" tab.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. In window 1, drag the card for {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  2. Straight away, in window 2, click "Create Invoice" and leave the "New Customer Payment" window open (closing it takes the invoice back off).
  3. Before the message closes (about 5 seconds), in window 1 click "Undo".
  4. Refresh window 1.
  5. Look at the card for {Work-order-1}.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 2: the work order is invoiced (window 2 shows it as Invoiced).
  • Step 3: the Undo is refused: {Work-order-1} does not go back to {Technician-A}'s column. If a message shows, write down its words.
  • Step 4: the board reloads.
  • Step 5: {Work-order-1} is in {Technician-B}'s column.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Please try again.” shows.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Invoiced or Paid status. An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”

Not yet checked against a build.

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11524)
